subject: Biotechnology
title: DNA: The Blueprint of Life
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on DNA: The Blueprint of Life.

hook.text: Every cell in your body carries two meters of DNA — packed into a nucleus six micrometers wide.

buildup.text: DNA stores information in a four-letter alphabet — A, T, C, G — arranged in a double helix.

discovery.text: The sequence of letters encodes proteins — molecular machines that do nearly every job in your body.

twist.text: Only about 1.5% of human DNA codes for proteins — the rest was once dismissed as junk but has roles too.

climax.text: Biotech's power comes from reading, writing, and editing this code — DNA is both data and program.

punchline.text: Four letters write every living thing — biotech learned to edit the text.

quiz.question: What percentage of human DNA codes for proteins?

details.summary: DNA is the molecule that stores genetic instructions for building and operating all living organisms. Its double helix structure, with complementary base pairs of adenine-thymine and guanine-cytosine, enables both information storage and faithful replication during cell division.
details.whyItMatters: DNA is the foundation of all biotechnology. Every application from gene editing to forensics to genetic testing depends on understanding how DNA encodes information, replicates, and directs the production of proteins that build and operate cells.
takeaways: DNA stores genetic information in sequences of four nucleotide bases: A, T, G, C
Complementary base pairing enables accurate replication during cell division
The human genome contains about 3 billion base pairs encoding roughly 20,000 genes

faq.question: How does DNA store biological information?
faq.answer: Information is encoded in the sequence of four bases along the DNA strand, similar to how binary code uses zeros and ones. Three-letter codons specify amino acids, and the sequence of amino acids determines protein structure and function.

faq.question: Why is the double helix structure so important?
faq.answer: The double helix with complementary base pairing means each strand contains the information to rebuild the other. During replication, the strands separate and each serves as a template for a new complementary strand, ensuring faithful information copying.
